title: Luingam Luikham: Custodian of Tangkhul Oral Literature and Customary Law
alternate_titles: Biography of Luingam Luikham: Cultural Custodian and Folklorist
Luingam Luikham: Preserving the Heritage of Wungram
subject: Biography (Jeevani), Folklore & Cultural Custodianship
notes: Biography celebrating Luingam Luikham and the pioneering Luikham family of folklorists who documented traditional customary jurisprudence (Wung Naga Okthot Mayonza), oral riddles, and folk epics.

front_matter.title_page: Luingam Luikham: Custodian of Tangkhul Oral Literature and Customary Law (2010)
front_matter.preface: Luingam Luikham and his family represent the premier folklore collectors and customary law codifiers of the Tangkhul nation. Their exhaustive field collections preserved hundreds of ancient folk songs, clan migration genealogies, and legal precedents before they could be eroded by rapid modernization.

chapters.title: The Quest for Tangkhul Oral Heritage
chapters.summary: Field expeditions across remote villages collecting songs, riddles, clan genealogies, and folklore.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Luingam Luikhamna Ukhrul, Kamjong, Somra, kala Phadangwui remote villages-li field research eina zatpingsaye. Ana traditional elders, folk singers, kala village court headmen eina interview saye. Ana audio recordings, written notebooks, kala sacred oral songs kazip-kasasaye. Ana theitserie: Hao culture oral tradition-li rich-lakna, chi preserve kasa compulsory-sai.
chapters.english_translation: Luingam Luikham undertook pioneering field expeditions across remote villages in Ukhrul, Kamjong, Somra, and Phadang. He interviewed elder bards, traditional singers, and customary court headmen. He recorded oral songs, transcribed clan genealogies, and documented customary court cases, realizing that preserving oral folklore was vital for the cultural survival of the Tangkhul people.
grammar_notes: Folklore collection methodology terminology in Tangkhul.
exercises: Why was field documentation essential for preserving Tangkhul heritage?

chapters.title: Codifying Customary Jurisprudence & Folklore Volumes
chapters.summary: Publishing foundational books on Tangkhul customary law, folk tales, and traditional proverbs.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: Ana TLS eina publication-wui vang books kasasaye: Hao Ngashan customary law, Tungtuktui (riddles), Hao-laa (folk songs), kala clan histories. Awui booksna modern legal courts, schools, kala researchers-li standard reference thada serve saye. Ana Tangkhul bhashali rich literary prestige miserie.
chapters.english_translation: Collaborating with the Tangkhul Literature Society, he published landmark works on customary law, folk riddles, traditional poetry, and clan migrations. His publications became standard reference manuals for customary courts, schools, and university researchers, bestowing immense literary prestige upon the language.
grammar_notes: Classification of Tangkhul folk literature genres.
exercises: What types of folk literature did Luingam Luikham document?

chapters.title: Inspiration for Future Generations of Scholars
chapters.summary: The enduring impact of his preservation work on contemporary Naga cultural consciousness.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: Luingam Luikhamwui work-na modern Tangkhul youth-li cultural pride kala identity-wui understanding miserie. Ukhrul-li ana setup kahai archives modern linguists kala researchers-li guide saye. Awui name Tangkhul literary history-li immortal guardian thada ngashan-leisara.
chapters.english_translation: Luingam Luikham's work instilled deep cultural pride and self-understanding in younger generations. The archives and documentation he established in Ukhrul continue to guide linguists and anthropological researchers worldwide. His name will forever be remembered as an immortal guardian of Tangkhul heritage.
grammar_notes: Memorial reverence and cultural guardianship phrasing.
exercises: Explain the role of cultural archives in maintaining community identity.

lines: This chapter illustrates quintessential Tangkhul cultural ethics, clan loyalty, and narrative style.
Standard literary Tangkhul is employed throughout, preserving classic oral idioms,
traditional honorifics, and vivid metaphorical descriptions.
